cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, and he opens by talking straight to God: "Preserve me, O God, for in You I take refuge." No warm-up, no small talk. That man knew where the shelter was BEFORE anybody even checked the weather.

cards.question: David calls the LORD his Lord. True or false: David says he still has a few good things of his own, even apart from God.
Then David turns from God to the people around him. Who does David say all his delight is in?

cards.text: But not everybody runs to God for refuge. Some people go chasing other gods, like sprinting after a bus that isn't even going your direction. Sweating. Waving. For WHAT?

cards.question: What does David say will multiply for the people who chase other gods?
True or false: David says he won't pour out the libations of blood for those other gods, and he won't even speak their names.

cards.text: Now David talks about his portion and his cup. Everybody else is eyeing the biggest cookie in the batch, and David's over here like, nah, I've got something WAY better.

cards.question: David says his chosen portion is the ___.

cards.text: David says God has made his lot secure, and the lines of his boundary have fallen in pleasant places. Nobody reads their lease and says PLEASANT, friend. Nobody. But David does.

cards.question: True or false: David is disappointed with the inheritance he's been given.

cards.text: So David says he will bless the LORD. And he's got a reason ready.

cards.question: David says he'll bless the LORD. What does David say the LORD does for him?

cards.text: Even at night, David says, his conscience instructs him. Me? At night in the junk drawer, my only advice came from the dead batteries next to me, and they couldn't even power a FLASHLIGHT.

cards.question: David says he has set the LORD always before him, and the LORD is at his right hand. Because of that, what does David say?

answers.text: He will not lose a battle

cards.question: With the LORD right beside him, David says his heart is ___ and his body will dwell ___.

cards.text: Then David looks past this life. He tells God that God will not abandon his soul to Sheol.

cards.question: David also says God won't let His Holy One see ___.

cards.text: Much later, Peter, one of Jesus' apostles, says David saw this coming. Peter says David was speaking about the resurrection of the Christ, whose body did not see decay (Acts 2:31).

cards.question: David's last line starts with something God has made known to him. What is it?

cards.text: On that path, God will fill David with joy in His presence, with eternal pleasures at His right hand. He started this song asking for shelter and ended it at the BEST seat in the house.

findings.problem: The bus joke ends with 'Sweating. Waving. For WHAT?' This tells the baker that chasing other gods gets you nothing. That rules out 'Their riches' and 'Their followers' on card 5 before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke puts David inside the cookie scene ('Everybody else is eyeing the biggest cookie in the batch, and David's over here like, nah'). That blends the cookie comparison with the Bible setting instead of keeping them as two separate images.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'land' is a near-match for David's portion. Verse 6 talks about his boundary lines and his inheritance, so a baker could argue that land is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card says the boundary lines fell in 'pleasant places' and calls out 'PLEASANT'. That gives away the answer to card 10, which asks whether David is disappointed with his inheritance.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'So David says he will bless the LORD' links verse 7 to verses 5–6 as a result, and 'he's got a reason ready' adds a reason. The text doesn't give either link.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'securely' is the only adverb among the five words. The other four, including 'afraid', 'alone' and 'restless', are adjectives. Because the word type differs, blank 2's right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the last word of the line ('see ___': decay, defeat or sorrow). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason it out. It tests wording they haven't seen.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'On that path, God will fill David with joy' joins the path of life to the joy in God's presence. Verse 11 only lists them side by side and doesn't connect them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
